title: The Damdami Taksal
hookLine: a school of recitation and exposition that traces itself to Baba Deep Singh

lines: A SCHOOL NAMED FOR A MINT.
cards: A coin from a careless mint looks almost right. The edge is a little soft, the face a little blurred, and after a while the shopkeepers start biting it to check.
A coin from a careful mint is crisp; every line is where it should be, and nobody has to bite it. Year one stood in the Japji's workshop, where the Word is struck in a true mint.
Today: a school with the word mint in its own name, one that sets out to strike readers of Gurbani as crisply as coins.

teach.b: Taksal means a mint, the place where coins are struck. The Japji uses it in its thirty-eighth step, on Ang 8, in paraphrase: in the true mint, the Word is struck.
The Damdami Taksal is a school of Sikh learning that carries that word in its name.

teach.h: A CHAIN BACK TO BABA DEEP SINGH.
teach.b: Damdami points to Damdama Sahib, at Talwandi Sabo, where year three sat at the desk with Baba Deep Singh, copying the Granth one letter at a time.

The Taksal traces its line of teachers back to him, and through him, in its own telling, to Guru Gobind Singh at Damdama: a chain of teacher to student, each handing on the same careful way of reading.
The school strikes three things, mainly.

teach.h: RECITATION, KATHA, A WAY OF LIFE.
teach.b: Recitation: reading Gurbani aloud, steadily and correctly. Exposition, which Sikhs call katha: explaining what the lines mean.
And the way of life around both, kept in the school itself, where students live and learn together.
The Taksal keeps its own rehat on some points, and Sikhs hold a range of views about where it and the wider panth's code agree and differ. Today stays with what it's known for: care.
Gurbani is meant to be heard and sung, not only read silently.

teach.h: A SLURRED WORD BLURS THE MEANING.
teach.b: A word slurred or misplaced can blur the meaning, the way a soft edge blurs a coin.
So the students repeat, and repeat, and are corrected, until the line comes out crisp. Tomorrow sits in on that teaching itself.

how: Students of the Damdami Taksal live and study together, learning to recite Gurbani correctly and to give katha; the school traces its line of teachers to Baba Deep Singh at Damdama Sahib.

games.q: a student at the Taksal slurs one word of a line. what does a school of careful reading do?
o: let it go; the meaning is close enough.
have the student repeat until the word comes out crisp.

practice: Take the opening of the Mool Mantar, two words you've heard many times on this path: Ik Onkar. Say it silently and slowly, Ik on the in-breath, Onkar on the out-breath, letting each sound land fully before the next.
If you pray, let the line itself be the prayer.
